To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Adolescents who watch more television are those who spend less time with friends and more time with family; adolescents who listen to more music are those who are more involved with peers, and spend less time with family.

the decrease in TV watching and increase in music consumption that occur during adolescence are attributable to the changing social ecology in which media use occurs: Adolescents spend more time with their friends than with their families, and they spend less time with their families than do preadolescents.
the shift from television to other media during early adolescence is attributable to a shift from a family to a peer orientation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which media use reflects the changing social ecology in which adolescents live.
the changing ecology of adolescent media use and the implications of these changes for the socialization of adolescents.
the social ecology of adolescents, and how their changing media use reflects their changing relationships with parents and peers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decline in television viewing is not simply a result of a decline in family time.
television viewing is not a "bad" activity for adolescents; rather, it is a good activity for preadolescents and a less appropriate activity for adolescents.

adolescents are not watching less television because they are listening more to music, but rather, they are watching less television because of the changing ecology of their daily lives, which includes less family time, and because of the developmental task of separating from parents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decline in TV viewing is associated with less time spent with the family and more time spent with peers.
adolescents are becoming more like adults, but not in the way that many adults might wish.
the shift from television to other media, particularly music, is not simply an individual choice, but is embedded in a larger social ecology of the family and friends.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the media choices of early adolescents reflect their changing relationships with family and friends.
the media ecology of adolescents is in flux, and that media choices may reflect changes in the social ecology of adolescents.
media use is embedded in the social ecology of daily life and is shaped by social contexts.
